META.subject: Core Mathematics
META.subtitleDoc: OpenAI-only evaluation • Sub-Strand 2.9 • 12 lessons • teacher review copy

UNIT.sep: Define signed quantities,construct graphs,interpret slopes/areas and bound conclusions by measured data/model assumptions.
UNIT.careers: Illustrative timing,transport-data and motion-model analysis;no driving,road-safety clearance or professional navigation certification.
UNIT.focus: Distance/displacement,speed/velocity,acceleration,displacement-time and velocity-time graphs,relative speed and honest measured-versus-supplied evidence.
UNIT.phenomenon: A fictional journey report reads graph height as speed,infers acceleration from one finish time and turns an ideal passing calculation into a safety claim.
UNIT.supportingPhenomena: Returning paths,unit conversions,timed safe motion,signed graph areas,closing/separating models and a passing-alignment diagram.
UNIT.drivingQuestion: What can a motion record actually establish about a journey? KICD: What is speed? How do we use displacement-time graphs in real life? How do we use velocity-time graphs?
UNIT.storylineThread: Path/change → units/averages → actual timing limits → displacement graph → interpretation → acceleration → velocity graph → signed areas → relative motion → passing limits → audit → independent evidence.
UNIT.coreCompetencies:
Communication and Collaboration: the learner discusses different displacement-time graphs.
Self-Efficacy: the learner participates in a race of a specified distance, record time taken by a learner and work out the velocity and acceleration.
Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: the learner observes two bodies in motion such as cars when overtaking or moving in opposite directions and works out the relative speed of the two bodies in motion.
UNIT.values:
Responsibility: as the learner uses objects in motion such as thrown objects and many others to explain distance, displacement, speed, velocity and acceleration.
Integrity: as the learner participates in a race of a specified distance, records time taken by each learner and accurately works out the velocity and acceleration of different learners
Unity: as the learner participates and collaborates in a race to record time taken by each learner and work out the velocity and acceleration of different learners.
UNIT.pcis:
Learner Support Programmes (Sports and Games): the learner participates in a race of a specified distance, records time taken by each learner and works out the velocity and acceleration,
Socio-Economic and Environmental Issues (Safety and Security): the learner observes the two bodies in motion such as cars when overtaking or moving in opposite directions and works out the relative speed of these two bodies in motion.
Road safety: as the learner observes two vehicles when one is overtaking, discusses and works out the relative speed of the two vehicles. Also discusses the dangers of careless overtaking.
UNIT.content: Distance, displacement, speed, velocity, and acceleration; Velocity and acceleration; Displacement time graph; Interpretation of displacement-time graph; Velocity time graph; Interpretation of velocity-time graph; Relative speed
UNIT.subject: Core Mathematics
UNIT.learningOutcomes:
explain the terms distance, displacement, speed, velocity and acceleration in real-life situations,
determine velocity and acceleration in different situations,
draw a displacement-time graph of different situations,
interpret displacement-time graph in different situations,
draw a velocity-time graph from given tables in different situations,
interpret velocity-time graph in different situations,
determine relative speed of two moving bodies in different situations,
appreciate use of linear motion in real-life situations.

FINAL_EXPLANATION.instructions: Lesson12,40minutes:4procedure,16sections1–2,12section3,4section4,4checking/collection. Work independently with LM12 and blank squared paper only. East is positive. Show labelled axes/units,slopes and signed versus magnitude areas. Straight interpolation is a supplied model assumption,not an observation of detailed real motion. No teaching cards,hints or peer discussion before collection.

sections.title: 1. Quantities and missing evidence
sections.prompt: Distinguish distance/displacement and average speed/velocity using a returning path example. Define acceleration with units. Explain why a separate timed activity giving only distance and total time cannot establish its acceleration without additional evidence or a justified model.
sections.exemplar: Distance sums path lengths;displacement is signed final-minus-initial position. A return can have nonzero distance and zero net change;average speed uses distance/time,velocity uses displacement/time. Acceleration is change in velocity/time,m/s². Distance/time alone gives an average rate,not initial/final velocity or how it changed;additional velocity observations/model needed.

sections.title: 2. Displacement-time construction and interpretation
sections.prompt: Draw datasetSwith labelled axes and the supplied interpolation. Find velocity on each interval,rest interval,total distance,net displacement,average speed and average velocity over6s. Explain why graph height is not speed.
sections.exemplar: Plot(0,0),(2,6),(4,6),(6,2). Slopes+3,0,−2m/s;rest2–4s. Distance6+0+4=10m,net+2m;averagespeed5/3m/s,averagevelocity1/3m/s. Height is displacement fromO;its time gradient is signed velocity.

sections.title: 3. Velocity-time construction and interpretation
sections.prompt: Draw datasetVand find acceleration on each interval. Locate the zero crossing and calculate net displacement and total distance,showing how below-axis area is treated. Explain the horizontal nonzero segment.
sections.exemplar: Plot(0,−2),(2,2),(4,2),(6,0). Slopes+2,0,−1m/s²;zeroatt1s. First negative/positive triangles each1m cancel for net0butadd2mfor distance;remaining areas4+2m. Net+6m,distance8m. Horizontalv2means constant eastward velocity,not rest.

sections.title: 4. Relative motion,use and limits
sections.prompt: For the LM12following objects,find closing speed and ideal catch-up time. State the direction/constant-speed assumptions. Give one concrete benefit of a checked graph/relative-rate result and one missing real-world fact that prevents treating it as a safe-overtaking permission.
sections.exemplar: Closing10−6=4m/s,time24/4=6s;AbehindB,same straight direction and constant speeds. A model can estimate a gap/meeting time or identify rest/reversal;link to a checked result. Vehicle lengths,gaps,visibility,oncoming traffic,response or route restrictions are not supplied;the mathematical result is not road permission or proof of practical driving competence.

lessons.title: Can a return journey have positive distance but small displacement?
lessons.observed: Returning motion adds distance while reducing net change.
lessons.learned: Average speed and velocity use different numerators.
lessons.explained: One travel time does not establish acceleration.

lessons.title: Which units belong in a velocity calculation?
lessons.observed: Rates need common units before comparison.
lessons.learned: Signed averages and instantaneous values are different claims.
lessons.explained: Unit cancellation supports a justified conversion.

lessons.title: What can a safe timed activity measure?
lessons.observed: Actual timed data contain uncertainty and action limits.
lessons.learned: Average motion can be calculated without claiming unmeasured acceleration.
lessons.explained: A source activity suggestion does not make missing velocity data available.

lessons.title: How does a displacement-time table become a graph?
lessons.observed: A flat displacement graph represents no position change.
lessons.learned: Signed slopes give velocities in the stated model.
lessons.explained: Distance and net displacement require different accumulation rules.

lessons.title: Is graph height the journey's displacement?
lessons.observed: The graph starts away from the chosen origin.
lessons.learned: Journey displacement is an ordinate difference.
lessons.explained: Height and slope encode different physical quantities.

lessons.title: Does negative acceleration always mean slowing?
lessons.observed: Positive acceleration can reduce a negative velocity's magnitude.
lessons.learned: Acceleration concerns signed velocity,not speed alone.
lessons.explained: Within-interval claims need an explicit motion assumption.

lessons.title: What do slope and area mean on a velocity graph?
lessons.learned: Height,slope and area have distinct meanings.
lessons.explained: Distance equals net displacement magnitude here because velocity never reverses.

lessons.title: How do we count area when velocity crosses zero?
lessons.observed: A short reversed interval contributes negative displacement but positive distance.
lessons.learned: Distance needs area splitting where velocity changes sign.
lessons.explained: Negative acceleration can increase speed after reversal.

lessons.title: Are the objects closing or separating?
lessons.observed: Opposite directions can produce approach or separation.
lessons.learned: Relative-speed magnitude and closing interpretation are different questions.
lessons.explained: Starting positions/directions determine how the gap changes.
